description: PostgreSQL provider extensions for EFCore.ComplexIndexes — GIN, GiST, BRIN, SP-GiST, and Hash index support for complex type properties.
releaseNotes:
The last 5.x minor with a change of its own: the line refuses EF Core 11, whose successor is CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit.PostgreSQL.

Changed answers

- Indexes: an IncludeProperties(…) entry that names neither a property nor a column of the table fails at migrations add. When its property was removed, the migration dropped only the column, and the index with it, and applied cleanly (#142 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/142), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#include-entries-must-name-a-column)).
- Expression indexes: typed expression indexes and typed filters render Substring, Trim, TrimStart and TrimEnd as EF Core's queries do, so those queries can use the indexes. Trim() also trims tabs and line breaks, where it trimmed spaces only, so a typed filter can cover other rows: x.Code.Trim() != "" leaves out a tabs-only value (#72 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/72), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#substring-and-trim-render-as-ef-cores-queries)).
- Expression indexes: a typed expression index or filter wraps a concatenated operand that can be null in COALESCE(…, ''), as EF Core's queries do. x.Code + x.Suffix was NULL for every row without a suffix, so a unique index skipped those rows (#94 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/94), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#concatenation-with-a-nullable-operand)).
- Filters: a typed filter keeps C#'s answer where an operand is null. x => x.Kind != "federated" on a string? covers the rows whose Kind is null, where it left them out, and a captured null compares with IS NULL, where it matched no row (#68 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/68), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#typed-filters-keep-cs-answer-for-null-operands)).
- Filters: a brace in a string literal of a typed filter is compared as written. x => x.Code != "{draft}" renders '{draft}', where it rendered '{{draft}}' and kept the rows the filter excludes (#70 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/70), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#typed-filters-keep-braces-in-string-literals)).
- Constraints: an exclusion constraint, temporal constraint or temporal foreign key declared on a TPC type is added to the table of every type derived from it. On a concrete base it was added to the base's table only, and the derived tables accepted the overlapping rows it refuses (#93 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/93), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).

Breaking

- Registration: UseNpgsqlComplexIndexes(), AddNpgsqlComplexIndexes() and the design-time registration dotnet ef runs throw InvalidOperationException on an EF Core major other than 10, naming CodoMetis.EFCore.SchemaKit for EF Core 11. EF Core 10 on .NET 11 keeps working (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#ef-core-11-is-refused-at-registration)).
- Indexes: a complex index, exclusion constraint or temporal constraint on a TPC type with derived types fails at migrations add when it reads a member of a complex property, which EF Core 10 maps to no column in a derived table; map the member as a regular property (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Constraints: a temporal foreign key to a TPC type with derived types fails at migrations add, since its rows live in several tables; reference a type with no derived types (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).

Changed

- Indexes: a complex index, exclusion constraint or temporal constraint declared on the abstract base of a TPC hierarchy is created on every concrete table, as EF Core's own indexes are, where it failed at migrations add (Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Indexes: an explicit name on a TPC type's complex index, exclusion constraint or temporal constraint stays on that type's table, and each derived table's copy takes the name followed by its table. A copy's name past the identifier limit is shortened as EF Core's are, a temporal foreign key's too (#145 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/145), #167 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/167), #168 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/168), Upgrading (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/upgrading.md#declarations-on-a-tpc-type-cover-every-table-of-the-hierarchy)).
- Packaging: each package carries the version's section of its changelog as its NuGet release notes, which nuget.org's Release Notes tab and Visual Studio's Updates tab show.
- Packaging: the release notes, the README on nuget.org and the GitHub release link the documentation at the version's tag, so they keep describing the version they shipped with after main moves on to the next line.
- Packaging: the PostgreSQL and SQL Server packages depend on exactly their own version of EFCore.ComplexIndexes, and the core differ refuses a satellite of another version, naming both. Update the packages together: a 5.4.x satellite beside core 5.5.0 was refused as the core differ (#169 (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/issues/169)).

Fixed

- Indexes: a complex index, exclusion constraint or temporal constraint named like a table, view or sequence of its schema, the sequence of an identity or serial column included, fails at migrations add, where it failed at apply with 42P07 (Index names (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/README.md#single-column-index-on-a-complex-property)).
- Expression indexes: a typed expression index or filter refuses a member of a scalar type, such as CreatedAt.Year, at the declaration, where it failed at migrations add. .Value and .HasValue on a nullable translate (Typed expression indexes (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-indexes.md#typed-linq-expression-indexes)).
- Filters: a typed filter compares a char with a char literal, where it failed at apply on the char's code, and x.RevokedAt.HasValue renders IS NOT NULL, where it failed at migrations add (Typed filters (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-indexes.md#typed-filters)).
- Filters: a filter of an index or exclusion constraint that compares a date or time ToJson() member with a column fails at migrations add, naming the member, where it failed at apply comparing text with a timestamp (JSON member indexes (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-indexes.md#json-member-indexes)).
- Constraints: a migration that drops both tables of a temporal foreign key applies, Down() included, where it failed with 2BP01 when the principal's table sorted first (Temporal foreign keys (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-constraints.md#temporal-foreign-keys-period--requires-postgresql-18)).
- Constraints: an exclusion constraint filter on a ToJson() number, boolean, uuid or enum member casts it as EF Core's queries do and applies, where it failed with 42883 or 42804 (Exclusion constraints (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-constraints.md#exclusion-constraints-exclude)).
- Constraints: an exclusion constraint with a scalar element under gist gets btree_gist whatever the element's operator and however the method is spelled, so <> and UseMethod("GiST") apply, where they failed with 42704 when the extension was missing (Exclusion constraints (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-constraints.md#exclusion-constraints-exclude)).
- Migrations: a complex index, exclusion or temporal constraint renamed away from a name the same migration gives to another object applies, where it failed with 42P07 because the renamed one still held the name. It is dropped before EF Core's operations and created after them, with any temporal foreign key referencing it (Index names (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/README.md#single-column-index-on-a-complex-property)).
- Docs: the temporal foreign key samples pass both type arguments to HasTemporalForeignKey, and compile (Temporal foreign keys (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-constraints.md#temporal-foreign-keys-period--requires-postgresql-18)).
- Docs: the PostgreSQL index guide says to pass a fractional storage parameter as a string, since Npgsql's generator formats numbers with the current culture (Index methods (https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/docs/postgresql-indexes.md#index-methods-on-a-complex-property)).

Full changelog: https://github.com/CaffeinatedCoder/EFCore.ComplexIndexes/blob/v5.5.0/src/EFCore.ComplexIndexes.PostgreSQL/CHANGELOG.md
